data.content_ref: inline:SRC_006 abstracts SRC_001–SRC_005 by identifying the covering principle: on random 3-regular graphs under asynchronous majority, the consensus probability is governed by whether the monotone cut-size descent reaches a jammed matching before the empty cut; the disagreement among the endpoints is a phase transition in graph expansion. Refuted if the final crossing-edge density is not a monotone function of the graph's expansion profile or if the cut size can increase under the dynamics.
